subject: Post-renewal usage spike and single-invoice recast request
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma.ross@novapulse.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected one-off charge after renewal

Hi Karthik / Monica,

We just received an invoice for a one-time charge of $48,200 covering a usage spike dated 2026-09-28 — after our renewal and capacity increase completed on 2026-09-01. This caught our finance team off guard. On renewal we upgraded committed capacity and expected overages to be handled under the new commit, not invoiced separately.

Can you share a breakdown of the spike (hours, regions, model variants) and confirm whether this should be a retroactive true-up or if it can be folded into our renewal commit? We'd like to avoid a separate large invoice if possible; if not, we need a short amortization plan and a corrected invoice we can route to procurement.

Attached: nova_spike_usage_report.csv (raw hourly consumption).

Thanks,
Emma Ross
Head of Platform Ops
NovaPulse
emma.ross@novapulse.com
+1 415-555-0136

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@novapulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-off charge after renewal

Emma — thanks for the flags and the CSV. I pulled this into our billing team and Ben/Monica are helping with the forensics. Initial read is that the spike originated from a short-lived burst in eu-west (model variant: gpt-s-8k-quant) that exceeded the commit window before routing fallback kicked in. That led to a one-off settlement invoice rather than being applied against the renewed commit.

Plan:
- Monica to validate the hourly split and confirm which hours were outside the committed quota.
- We will produce a single reconciled invoice that either: (A) reclassifies the charge as a post-renewal true-up and offsets it against the monthly commit going forward, or (B) remains a one-off invoice but we apply a partner credit as a courtesy and offer amortization.

Could you confirm NovaPulse's preference between (A) folding into the commit (preferred by us if the spike is legitimate usage tied to the renewal) vs (B) a short-term amortized charge? If you prefer (A) we'll need a short acceptance to amend the commit accounting on your side so procurement can close the loop.

Attaching: oneoff_invoice_draft.pdf for transparency — placeholder until Monica confirms line-items.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@novapulse.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-off charge after renewal

Emma — I validated the CSV and pulled hour-by-hour token/instance metrics. Short summary:

- Spike window: 2026-09-28 02:00–07:00 UTC.
- Region: primarily eu-west (88% of the extra hours).
- Model variant: gpt-s-8k-quant with burst scaling to additional workers due to a concurrent batch process.
- Committed capacity hit: yes — the automated fallback that should have routed to our reserved pool lagged due to a transient control-plane throttling event; that's on us.

Recommendation:
1) We can reissue a reconciled invoice that nets the excessive hours against a one-time 30% goodwill credit (applied because this was a routing failure on Redwood's side). New net one-off charge: $33,740.
2) Offer an amortization schedule across next 3 invoices to soften cashflow: see amortization_schedule.xlsx (attached).
3) Or, if you prefer to fold it into the commit (method A), we can amend the renewal paperwork to adjust effective committed hours and remove the invoice entirely; that requires an acknowledgement from procurement/finance that they're comfortable with a commit amendment versus a separate financial charge.

Let me know which path NovaPulse prefers. If you pick amortization, Ben will trigger a corrected invoice (PDF) and I will add a line-item note referencing the control-plane routing issue.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Finance Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@novapulse.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected one-off charge after renewal — agreed path forward

Emma — quick follow-up to confirm the resolution we discussed with finance and procurement today. Per your note (confirmed offline with procurement): NovaPulse prefers an amortized one-off invoice rather than amending the signed commit. Below is the agreed path and next steps.

Agreed settlement (summary):
- Original one-off: $48,200
- Goodwill credit: 30% ($14,460) applied due to control-plane routing lag
- Net settlement: $33,740 to be amortized over 3 monthly invoices (11/2026, 12/2026, 01/2027) — see amortization_schedule.xlsx attached.
- Redwood will reissue the invoice as a single corrected PDF with line-item notes and a reference code RDW-4381-SETTLE. Ben will send the PDF to your AP inbox within 24 hours.
- DocuSign link for a short acceptance (acknowledgement of the amortization schedule and closure of dispute): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123

If procurement needs any alternate billing terms (Net30 vs Net45) please reply to Ben directly (ben.carter@redwoodinference.com). Once signed, we will mark the ticket resolved and route a final reconciliation report.

Thanks for working through this — and apologies again for the disruption.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
